title: AI scams in Georgia and South Florida: How scammers use deepfakes to steal millions

reading.body:
Criminals used generative AI to create deepfakes, cloned voices, and false identities to defraud people in Georgia and South Florida, including targeting immigrants with fake legal services from impersonated attorneys. This is a failure of identity verification at the point where victims encountered the scammers. The scams succeeded because victims had no reliable way to confirm they were communicating with legitimate professionals rather than AI-generated imposters.

The deployment failure was in social platforms and communication channels that did not prevent spoofed phone numbers, cloned voices, or fabricated profiles from reaching potential victims. Catching these scams would have required either victims to verify contacts through independent trusted channels, or platforms to implement identity verification that distinguished real professionals from AI impersonations.

It is not established whether the platforms hosting these scams were aware of the fraudulent activity, or what specific AI systems were used to generate the deepfakes and voices.

summary:
Criminals are increasingly using artificial intelligence to create realistic deepfakes, cloned voices, and fake identities to commit scams across Georgia and South Florida. According to the FBI's 2025 Internet Crime Report, Americans lost nearly $893 million to AI-enabled scams last year. Specific cases include a South Florida immigration attorney whose voice and identity were cloned to target immigrants, and a Cobb County couple who lost approximately $800,000 in a cryptocurrency scam. Florida reported 350 AI-related complaints with $39.9 million in losses, while Georgia recorded 71 complaints with $10.4 million in losses, though these figures likely undercount the actual problem.

Scammers use generative AI to clone voices from social media, spoof phone numbers, create fake photos, and research family relationships to make scams more convincing. Common schemes include the grandparent scam, romance scams, and fake emergency calls. Financial institutions warn customers to verify requests through trusted channels and avoid responding immediately to unexpected communications. The Georgia Attorney General recommends families establish secret code words to verify identity during emergencies. As AI tools become cheaper and more accessible, investigators predict these scams will continue evolving, making verification procedures a critical defense against fraud.
